characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the chemical composition of the VIM Fe-7Al ingot (feedstock for the cold-rolled sheets/foils).
characterization_methods.technique: chemical analysis (elemental composition); hydrogen gas analysis

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 50-kg capacity, 125-kW medium-frequency chamber vacuum induction furnace; alumina-lined crucible of approximately 150 mm diameter and 300 mm height; soft iron pieces charged at bottom with aluminum pieces on top; evacuated to 10^-4 torr; melt poured at 1893 K into 80-mm-diameter split cast iron molds kept inside the vacuum chamber; resulting VIM Fe-7Al ingot sound and free from microcracks and hydrogen gas porosity.
80-mm-diameter VIM ingot preheated in a hearth furnace at 1373 K for 1 h and hot-forged in a 1-tonne pneumatic forge hammer with die platens at room temperature.

24-mm-thick sections of forged billets preheated at 1373 K for 1 h and hot rolled by 50% with 1-mm reduction in thickness per pass; reheated after every six rolling passes; final thickness of hot-rolled plate 12 mm.
Fe-7 wt.% Al alloy produced by VIM could be cold rolled to thin sheets and foils (Fig. 3). No specific cold-rolling reduction, temperature or pass schedule is reported for the VIM condition.

unmapped_findings: Fe-7 wt.% Al alloy produced by VIM (and AIMFC) could be cold rolled to thin sheets and foils; however, no separate tensile data are reported in this paper for the cold-rolled VIM condition — the only cold-rolled tensile table (Table III) is for the AIMFC cold-rolled-and-annealed 2-mm sheet. [b0041, b0042]
The VIM Fe-7Al ingots were sound and completely free from microcracks as well as hydrogen gas porosity. [b0018]
VIM provides better control of chemical composition and recovery of alloying additions; very low levels of impurities could be achieved in VIM. [b0021]
Aluminum recovery during VIM is 96–98%, comparable to the AIMFC recovery of 95–98%. [b0025]
